Oh, you know, I have to say, and not to make it super political, but I will say having sat as a ranking member for subcommittee on Homeland Security, I see a lot of the challenges that don't make front page news. Our open border in along the Southwest region is our biggest national security threat today. And I say that because in the last year alone, we have seen over two dozen known individuals on the international terrorist watch list being apprehended. We have seen a dramatic, and I mean, I can't emphasize this enough, a dramatic increase In cartel illegal activity along the border building up networks with with resources that are rivaling that of the the government of Mexico. I mean, when you look at the smuggling operation that is occurring at the southwest border. That is a $32 million a day of what we are seeing. And that is absolutely incredible amount of money that is being made by the cartels, which is empowering them to continue building up networks, building up infrastructure. And when you don't have a secure border, you don't have a secure nation. When we only have 10% of all of our commercial cargo being inspected at random, Then it's just a numbers game, what is being smuggled through, you could have everything from pests and diseases that in fact are domestic production of agricultural crops or livestock that could wipe out an entire industry just by. lack of having enough inspectors at the border. When you look at the weapons that can be smuggled in, the dirty bombs, things like this, these are all things that keep me up at night having seen firsthand the gaps that we have in terms of border security. And of course, border security isn't just limited to the Southwest border. It's our ports as well. And so our ports play an important role in how we manage what's coming in and making sure that we're protecting industry here at home while still maintaining an efficient flow of commerce and goods and services that are coming through. And I gotta give a shout out of course to our coast, our coasties because nobody does port security better than the coast guard. And they're hugely, hugely important to the maritime industry. So always looking to work, looking forward to working with men because whether it's LNG, whether it is, you know, port security, national security, it is always remarkable to see what they're up to. But beyond that, beyond the terrifying border situation that we're facing, I do think we have a real serious threat in our debt. We are on an unsustainable path currently when you see in 2021, we spent close to $7 trillion. We're garnishing the wages of our kids, our grandkids, but every American is facing an inflation tax today because of this government spending. And then, of course, you look at the global context of what is happening in Russia, Ukraine, and, of course, China. China would love nothing more than to see America taking off the world stages as the world's leading superpower. But I'm sure your listeners and your viewers would probably not sleep well if I kept going. So we have plenty of challenges, but I remain optimistic that we will handle them with flying colors and be better on the other side of it for having faced them.
